summary: John's 7th-great-grandfather, father of Keturah Tuttle Lamoreaux; a Brookhaven-born Tuthill who moved to Woodbury Clove in the Orange County, NY highlands.
bio:
Alva M. Tuttle's 1968 compilation (p. 311, quoted on WikiTree Tuthill-364 and Smith-141655) reads: 'JOHN TUTHILL ~1730 Brookhaven, LI s Jas 1692; d ~1770 Woodbury Clove, Orange, NY; m 23Nov1752 Smithtown, LI Temp d ~1780 da Jas & Jerusha (TOPPING) SMITH.' Children: twins James & John (1753), twins Ezekiel & William (c.1754), Keturah (~1755), Samuel and Daniel. His father James Tuthill (b. ~1692 Oysterponds) moved from Brookhaven to Ulster/Orange between 1742 and 1748. The Woodbury Clove militia company of 1775–76 was commanded by Capt. Francis Smith, with Thomas Smith 1st lt. and (1776) Thos. Lammoreux ensign; the Upper Clove company had been commanded by Capt. Austin Smith; Austin, Francis and Jeremiah are exactly the sons of James Smith & Jerusha Topping, i.e. Temperance's brothers. The 1775 Articles of Association in Cornwall Precinct were signed by 'Thomas Lamoureux' and 'James Tuttle' (probably John's son James, b. 1753). The 'Capt.' title: S. W. Eager, Outline History of Orange County (1846), pp. 527–529, lists 'Capt. J. Tuthill' among Cornwall precinct officers, records that in 1769 the justices cancelled the indenture of apprentice James Simmons 'by the ill-treatment of his master, John Tuthill', and names a 'Capt. Tuthill' on a 1788 committee (too late for a John who died c.1770; possibly son John b. 1753). Ruttenber also lists 'Clove Co.—1775—Jonathan Tuthill, captain.' The deep-dive report found 'no evidence of the title'. The Hauppauge report found no trace of John or Temperance in Smithtown records and noted that the 23 Nov 1752 Smithtown wedding came from an unsourced online tree (My Maine Heritage); Round 2 then found it in Alva Tuttle (1968). If Temperance was raised in Moriches, the couple most plausibly lived in Brookhaven before moving to Orange County; a possible migration vehicle is Rev. Abner Reeve's 1763 removal 'with a company of emigrants' from Moriches to Blooming Grove (possible). The tree had merged him with a James M. Tuthill & Hannah S. Reeve parentage (wrong: that couple is Joshua Tuthill & Hannah Reeve).

Two new pieces bear on John's life. First, a 'John Tuthill' signed the 1775 Articles of Association in Cornwall Precinct, on the same list as 'James Tuttle' and Thomas Lamoureux ([R4-S3]). Either John was still alive in 1775, which would undercut Alva Tuttle's c.1770 death and partly vindicate the tree's later death date, or the signer was his son John (b. 1753). Second, the Brookhaven town records show the family's Long Island base. James Tuthill, John's probable father, held the westernmost 15-acre lot in Fireplace Neck by 1737 ([R4-S2]). That is a few miles from Moriches, where Temperance Smith's father James Smith lived, so the two families were close neighbours.

The printed pre-1784 New York marriage-license list has no Tuthill-Smith entry ([R4-S4]), and the NY will abstracts to 1784 hold no will or administration for him ([R4-S6]). The 23 Nov 1752 Smithtown marriage date therefore still rests on Alva Tuttle alone. It is repeated without sources by Long Island Surnames ([R4-S5]) and in an Ancestry compiled index cited on WikiTree.

Round 4 relationship evidence (parent I282608055692, probable): Unchanged: rests on Alva Tuttle p. 311 ('s Jas 1692'). New context: James Tuthill owned land in Fireplace Neck, Brookhaven, 1721-1750, and a 'James Tuttle junr.' appears there c.1738/9, consistent with Alva's son James b. 1717.

Round 4 searched without result: NY marriage licenses before 1784 (1860 printed list, full text): no Tuthill/Tuttle-Smith license; no Lamoreaux-Tuthill license; Abstracts of Wills, NY Surrogate (NYHS Collections), all volumes 1730-1784 on archive.org, full text: no will or administration for John Tuthill of Cornwall/Woodbury Clove, James Tuthill (d. c.1772) or Temperance Tuthill; no will of James Smith of Moriches; FamilySearch published tree: no PID found via web search; Smithtown First Presbyterian Church marriages of 1751-53 (Rev. Napthali Daggett): no published transcription found
Round 4: Brookhaven town records place James Tuthill in Fireplace Neck near Moriches; found a John Tuthill among the 1775 Cornwall signers; marriage licenses and will abstracts negative.
